subject: Handoff: Quality-monitoring + canary/rollback plan for Aurelia deployment
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@aureliahealth.com>

Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: QMon kickoff + canary expectations

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are ready to move from pilot to limited roll‑out for our patient triage assistant next month. Before we lock in the schedule, we need a short handoff to your CS/implementation team that covers: prompt set validation, regression alerts cadence, and what a canary + rollback actually looks like operationally.

High level constraints: the assistant handles PHI-lite content (no raw PHI stored), response latency must stay below 600ms p95 for short queries, and we need automatic rollback if error rates spike >3% for more than 5m.

Can you put together a one‑pager and the initial prompt sets so our security and SRE folks can review? Priya is the technical lead at Aurelia — cc'd.

Thanks,
Samir
Sr. Product Manager, Aurelia Health

Attachments: none (we referenced the pilot report in the Deck)

Date: Mon, 03 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: QMon kickoff + canary expectations — handoff to CS/Implementation

Marissa/Ben —

Pls own this handoff. Aurelia is moving to limited roll out and wants a crisp plan covering: prompt sets, eval harness integration, regression alert thresholds, and canary + rollback playbook. Key constraints from Samir: p95 latency <600ms, auto rollback if error rate >3% for >5m.

I started a short scope doc and attached the prompt sets CSV (initial). The ask for your first pass:
- Review the attached prompt_sets_initial.csv and mark any problematic prompts (privacy/fallacy risk).
- Propose an eval harness checklist (what automatic tests to run pre‑canary).
- Draft canary metrics and rollback gates (who approves manual vs. automatic rollback).
- Provide an estimated timeline for a 2‑phase canary (10% / 100%) and what monitoring dashboards we need.

CC Laura to coordinate the SRE contact and request the audit log exports. Samir/Priya — Marissa will follow up with a proposed plan by EOD 7/5.

Thanks,
Diego
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: prompt_sets_initial.csv (12 rows)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@aureliahealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Jul 2028 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: QMon kickoff + canary expectations — handoff to CS/Implementation

Diego —

Quick update and plan attached (Aurelia_QMon_Scope_v1.pdf). Summary highlights:

1) Prompt sets: I reviewed the CSV. 2 prompts flagged for hallucination risk (rows 6 and 9); suggestions included stricter system role framing and adding explicit refusal templates. We recommend a prompt freeze for the canary window.

2) Eval harness: propose a two‑tier harness — unit-level synthetic tests (1000 prompt/response pairs, including adversarial cases) and shadow A/B evaluation against pilot traffic to measure latency, token cost, and answer fidelity. Include exact test scripts and expected baselines in the doc.

3) Regression alerts: set immediate alerts for (a) model error rate (API 5xx or invalid response) >2% over 3m, (b) fidelity regression measured by eval harness score drop >6% vs. baseline, (c) p95 latency >650ms sustained for 5m. Alert triage route: CS -> SRE -> Product on-call.

4) Canary + rollback: recommend a staged canary: 
   - Stage 1: 5% traffic for 24h with enhanced logging and manual check at 12h.
   - Stage 2: 25% for 24h if Stage 1 metrics green.
   - Auto rollback if model error rate >3% for 5m OR eval harness fidelity drop >8% at end of a 1h window.
   - Manual rollback gate: any security/compliance flag raised by Aurelia's reviewers.

5) Timeline: propose start 7/14 for Stage 1 (gives Aurelia one week to review).

Asks for Aurelia: share the SRE contact and a sample of live logs (anonymized) so we can configure the alert thresholds against real distributions.

Samir/Priya — please confirm the timeline and whether we can start the unit tests on your sandbox tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurelia_QMon_Scope_v1.pdf
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@aureliahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@aureliahealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Jul 2028 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: QMon kickoff + canary expectations — handoff to CS/Implementation

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. Timeline looks good; we can provide an anonymized log export by EOD 7/8 and our SRE lead (rohit.sre@aureliahealth.com) will join the validation meeting. A couple clarifications:
- Can you include an explicit table of rollback owners and escalation contacts? (we need names for our change control)
- For the eval harness, will Redwood run the shadow A/B or will Aurelia need to spin that up?

We are fine with the two‑phase canary but would prefer Stage 1 = 10% for 12h if Redwood is comfortable with the shorter window; otherwise we accept your 24h.

Priya
Technical Lead, Aurelia Health
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: QMon kickoff + canary expectations — handoff to CS/Implementation

Quick internal note —

Marissa: I'll own the eval harness execution and dashboarding. Action items for me:
- Spin up the synthetic unit test suite and run baseline against your CSV by 7/9.
- Implement the shadow A/B runner in staging (Redwood will run it; Aurelia just needs to enable traffic mirror).
- Add the rollback owner table to the scope doc and include pager/emails for automatic escalation.

On the traffic %: I'm OK with Priya's 10% for 12h as Stage 1 provided we keep the enhanced logging/verbose traces. If anything looks odd we flip the auto rollback immediately.

I'll drop a follow up with the dashboard links and the Drive folder where we will drop the synthetic results.

-ben
